content.text: I selected one approved data source and started ingestion. The dataset size was around 9 GB. I can't see any progress in the UI. It just says acquiring approved assets

I’m using the debugging workflow to trace the live job from the UI through the ingestion API and worker before changing anything. I’ll check whether bytes are being downloaded but not reported, or whether the worker is actually stalled; then I’ll make progress visible without overstating what the backend knows.

The first localization result is clear: the UI is polling correctly, but the job contract only exposes a coarse state and message. During a multi-gigabyte download, the worker writes the staging file without persisting byte counts, so “Acquiring approved assets” can remain unchanged for hours even when data is flowing. I’m checking the actual job/staging state next to distinguish slow progress from a stopped worker.

The live ingestion is not stalled: it has completed 40 of 42 selected archives—about 8.57 GB of 8.98 GB—and is actively writing the next archive. The UI is misleading because completed-asset receipts are persisted, but neither the API nor frontend exposes them as progress. I’m implementing progress from those durable receipts plus the active stream byte count, so reloads show real values rather than a simulated spinner.

I can fix this without touching or restarting the active download. I’m using the incremental implementation skill to expose the worker’s existing per-asset receipts in the frontend first; that keeps the displayed percentage auditable (“verified bytes”), works after reload, and avoids pretending we know bytes still buffered in the current file.

The download has now finished: all 42 assets and 8.98 GB were verified. The job subsequently failed during deterministic mapping or TimeF validation, so there is a second issue beyond the missing progress display. I’m preserving that evidence and locating the exact validation failure rather than treating the completed download as a successful ingestion.

The 8.98 GB download has finished and remains cached. I found a second issue after transfer: the importer expected one combined KUKA archive, while Zenodo provides 42 batch archives. I’m extending that specialized importer now so a retry can reuse the cached files and complete instead of downloading them again.
